indications: Acute exacerbation of COPD with hypercapnic respiratory failure (pH < 7.35, PaCO2 > 6.0 kPa / 45 mmHg)
Acute cardiogenic pulmonary oedema (severe dyspnoea, orthopnoea, pulmonary rales)
Immunocompromised patients with acute hypoxic respiratory failure
Post-extubation respiratory failure prevention in high-risk patients
contraindications: Severely impaired consciousness (GCS < 10) / inability to protect airway
Uncooperative, severely agitated, or somnolent patient
High aspiration risk, persistent vomiting, or bowel obstruction
Haemodynamic instability, shock, or severe uncorrected arrhythmias
Craniofacial trauma, facial burns, or anatomical deformity preventing mask seal

management_steps.details: Manage patient in the Resuscitation Area. Attach continuous cardiac monitoring, non-invasive BP (NIBP), and pulse oximetry.
Sit patient upright (> 45°). Reassure and explain the procedure clearly to the patient and family to reduce anxiety.
Select the appropriate size oro-nasal or full-face mask. Secure straps gently without excessive pressure to prevent skin breakdown.
CPAP mode: Start 5–10 cmH2O (for Pulmonary Oedema). BiPAP mode: Start IPAP 10–12 cmH2O, EPAP 4–5 cmH2O (for COPD). Titrate FiO2 to achieve SpO2 88–92% (COPD) or > 94%.
Repeat VBG/ABG after 1 hour. If pH improves and PaCO2 drops, continue NIV. If patient deteriorates, becomes somnolent, or SpO2 drops, proceed to ETT intubation.

warnings: Failure of NIV is an indication for immediate invasive mechanical ventilation (ETT intubation).
protocol.disposition: High Care / ICU admission for patients requiring ongoing NIV support.
